Text: The FAA said Friday that a software glitch affecting certain flight computers on Boeing’s 737 Max 10 is not a flight-safety concern, removing a key regulatory hurdle for certification of the aircraft. Following a review by FAA safety experts, the agency’s Corrective Action Review Board determined that pilots retain full control of the aircraft despite the software issue. The FAA also said the indications provided to flight crews are clear and unambiguous, supporting its conclusion that the glitch does not represent a safety risk. The decision is an important step toward certification of the 737 Max 10, Boeing’s largest Max variant, as the company seeks to advance the aircraft’s entry into commercial service. Certification of the jet has been closely watched by Boeing and airlines that have placed orders for the model. $BA

Text: Boeing is nearing a key regulatory milestone as the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration prepares to approve the 737 MAX 10, according to Bloomberg. Approval of the largest aircraft in the 737 MAX narrowbody family could be announced as early as next week. The certification would represent a strategic milestone for Boeing as it seeks to strengthen its competitive position against Airbus. Airlines are increasingly considering the high-capacity MAX 10 as a replacement for aging Boeing 757 fleets on busy domestic and transcontinental routes. Text: $BA My thoughts on BA. I regretted buy for me, but not quite enough to make a difference in the grand scheme. You have to take their quarterly reports with a grain of salt. Single quarter performance is not a great way to judge Boeing. Planes can take weeks to build. Put simply, cash is paid at delivery, not when the plane is built. A plane finished on September 29 but delivered October 2 shifts cash from one quarter to the next. Boeing’s total backlog reached a record $745 billion at the end of Q3 2026, and it includes more than 6,300 commercial airplanes. That sells them out until the earlt 2030s.
